extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent representatives/attorneys, national industrial property offices and ARIPO member state authorities
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/substantive standards for filing, examination, grant/registration, and post-grant administration of ARIPO patents, utility models and industrial designs under the Harare Protocol and its Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARIPO competence to grant and administer rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The African Regional Intellectual Property Organization (ARIPO) is empowered to grant patents and to register utility models and industrial designs and to administer such patents, utility models and industrial designs on behalf of Contracting States in accordance with the provisions of the Protocol, through its Secretariat (the Office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights granted/registered by ARIPO shall be called ARIPO patents/utility models/industrial designs and shall in each designated Contracting State have the effect of, and be subject to the same conditions as, a national patent/utility model/design granted/registered by that State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation: one or more Contracting States
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant of an ARIPO patent or the registration of an ARIPO utility model or an ARIPO industrial design may be requested for one or more of the Contracting States; designation is subject to payment of a designation fee and may be withdrawn at any time subject to payment of a prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must pay designation fees for each Contracting State designated; withdrawals of designation follow prescribed fee rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and representation: where and by whom
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall be filed by the authorized representative of the applicant or by the applicant with either the Office or, where the law of a Contracting State so permits, the industrial property office of a Contracting State; where applicant's residence/principal place of business is not situated in a Contracting State or the host country, the applicant shall be represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application filed with a national office has same effect as filing with Office; if filed with a national office it must be transmitted to the Office within 1 month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be lodged in any language which must be translated into English within 2 months from the date of filing in accordance with Rule 5(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants filing in languages other than English must ensure timely translation to avoid formal objection or refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority rights and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who previously applied in a Paris Convention member or WTO member enjoy a right of priority for 12 months (patents and utility models) and 6 months (industrial designs) from the date of filing the first application; multiple priorities may be claimed and time limits run from the earliest priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A declaration of priority and any other required documents must be filed per Implementing Regulations; multiple priorities may be claimed even if originating in different countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARIPO patent application unity and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked that they form a single general inventive concept; it shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art, entirely effected by an enabling description read with drawings if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must include a request for grant, description, claim(s), drawings (where necessary), sequence listing (where necessary) and an abstract; claims must be clear, concise and supported by the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims define protection; clarity and support
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought. They shall be clear and concise and shall be supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extent of protection is determined by the terms of the claims, but description and drawings shall be used to interpret the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract shall merely serve for use as a source of technical information; in particular not for the purposes of interpreting the scope of the protection sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should draft abstracts as technical summaries only; abstracts do not limit claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing of patent and utility model applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall publish ARIPO patent and utility model applications as soon as possible after expiry of 18 months from the date of filing or, if priority claimed, from the date of priority; publication may be earlier at applicant’s request subject to a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent/utility model is granted/registered before the 18-month period expires, publication may coincide with the grant/registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party observations after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Following publication of the ARIPO patent or utility model application, any third party may, in accordance with the Implementing Regulations, present observations concerning the patentability of the invention; that person shall not be a party to the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties may submit written observations on patentability; procedures and timelines governed by Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal and physical requirements examination and filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall examine whether the formal and physical requirements for applications as laid down in the Implementing Regulations and Administrative Instructions have been complied with and, if so, shall accord the appropriate filing date; if not complied with the Office shall notify the applicant inviting compliance within a prescribed period and may refuse the application if not remedied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet formal/physical requirements; notifications give opportunity to correct within prescribed timelines; failure leads to refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination and grounds for refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall, on request, undertake or arrange for substantive examination; if it finds that the invention claimed does not comply with requirements of patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial application), it shall refuse the application and notify the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can request substantive examination; refusal is notified and applicant may request reconsideration or appeal to the Board of Appeal per prescribed periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated State communication and 6-month response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office decides to grant a patent it shall notify the applicant and each designated State; each designated State shall have 6 months to respond that the patent shall have no effect in its territory for reasons such as the invention not being patentable under this Protocol or national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated State objections must be communicated within 6 months; applicants may respond with amendments/arguments within prescribed periods; if State persists in refusal, applicant may request national treatment in that State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments: applicant opportunity and no added matter
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or owner shall be allowed at least one opportunity of amending the description, claims and drawings of his own volition; an ARIPO application or patent may not be amended such that it contains subject-matter which extends beyond the content of the initial application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for admissibility of amendments shall be stipulated in the Regulations; amendments that add new matter are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability substantive requirements: novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO patents shall be granted for inventions in all fields of technology provided that they are new, involve an inventive step and are susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty: not anticipated by prior art. Inventive step: not obvious to a person skilled in the art. Industrial applicability: can be made or utilized in any kind of industry including agriculture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art definition and special exhibitions exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything made available to the public anywhere in the world by written disclosure, oral disclosure, use or exhibition before the filing date (or priority date) shall be considered prior art; disclosure at an official or officially recognized exhibition shall not be taken into consideration if it occurred not more than 6 months before filing (or priority date). Also, ARIPO patent applications filed earlier but published later are considered part of prior art for intervening filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of global disclosures and the 6-month grace for official exhibitions; earlier-filed ARIPO applications published later can form prior art against subsequent filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from patentability (subject-matter as such)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall not be regarded as inventions: discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods; aesthetic creations; schemes, rules and methods for performing mental acts, playing games or doing business, and programs for computers; presentations of information. This exclusion applies only to the extent that applications relate to such subject-matter 'as such.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting should emphasize technical character/technical contribution beyond excluded subject-matter to seek patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute exclusions (ordre public, biologicals, medical methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO patents shall not be granted in respect of: inventions whose commercial exploitation would be contrary to 'ordre public' or morality; plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes for production of plants or animals (excluding microbiological processes or products thereof); methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy and diagnostic methods practised on the human or animal body (excluding products for use in any of these methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants in biotech/medical fields must consider these exclusions and may claim product claims where permissible (e.g., products for use in methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term and maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent granted by the Office shall, provided it is maintained, have the same effect in each designated State as a national patent; the duration of the patent shall be 20 years from the filing date. On each anniversary of filing the Office shall collect prescribed annual maintenance fees; amount depends on number of States for which the application or patent is maintained and part of fees distributed among designated States as provided in Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/owners must pay annual fees to keep applications/patents in force; distribution and amounts per Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO divisional application may be filed directly with the Office only in respect of subject matter which does not extend beyond the scope of an earlier application as filed; it shall be deemed filed on the date of the earlier application and enjoy same priority. All Contracting States designated in the earlier application at time of filing shall be deemed to be designated in the divisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional cannot add new matter and preserves filing date/priority of earlier application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of protection determined by claims; use of description/drawings for interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of the protection conferred by an ARIPO patent or application shall be determined by the terms of the claims. Nevertheless, the description and drawings shall be used to interpret the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are primary for scope; ensure claims are consistent with description and drawings for correct interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT international applications treated as ARIPO applications (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application in which a Contracting State which is also bound by the PCT is designated for obtaining a patent under this Protocol shall be considered to be an application for grant under this Protocol; PCT provisions apply in addition to this Protocol and in case of conflict PCT provisions prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may act as receiving, designated, or elected Office under PCT in specified circumstances; certain time limits (e.g., payment of maintenance fees) are adjusted in relation to PCT Articles 22/39.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model is defined as a form, configuration or disposition of elements of some appliance, working tools and implements... in so far as they are capable of contributing some benefit or new effect or saving in time, energy and labour or allowing a better or different functioning; includes micro-organism or other self-replicable material, products of genetic resources, herbal as well as nutritional formulations which give new effects. A utility model shall be protected if it is new and industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility model applications must contain a request, description, claim(s), drawings and abstract, and are subject to formal and substantive examination; duration 10 years from filing; conversion to patent application allowed once before refusal/registration upon payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model application procedures and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall examine formal requirements and undertake substantive examination; if compliant, filing date accorded. The Office shall publish ARIPO utility model applications after 18 months from filing (or priority date) or earlier at applicant's request subject to fee; designated States have 6 months to object similarly to patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar procedural protections as patents apply for utility models including notifications, responses, and possible national treatment requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design application content and novelty requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for registration of an industrial design shall contain a request for registration and a reproduction of the industrial design and be subject to prescribed fees. A designated State may object within 6 months on grounds such as the industrial design not being new or national law making it unregistrable or textile designs being on a special register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration duration generally 15 years from filing (subject to national variations); annual maintenance fees apply; registrations subject to national law on compulsory licences/use in public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Appeal: composition, quorum, and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board of Appeal is established consisting of five members experienced in IP matters (two patent examiners); at all sittings at least one patent examiner must be present; three members form a quorum; functions include considering appeals from applicants, reviewing final administrative decisions of the Office and deciding other related matters; Board decisions shall be final and the Board may adopt its own rules of procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may appeal Office decisions to the Board within prescribed periods; Board's decisions are final under the Protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural forms and recordal requirements (assignments, licences, changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific ARIPO forms (e.g., Form Nos. 41–49) must be used for matters such as recordal of assignment/transmission, application to register licence or similar right, notice of recordal/change of applicant details, request for extension of time limits, grant of extension, notification of withdrawal/reduction of designated States, acknowledgement of receipt, request for expedited/delayed examination, and communication by designated State of acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms require specified accompanying documents (e.g., original or certified copy of assignment, licence contract) and signatures; fees and deadlines (e.g., payment within 21 days for extension requests) are prescribed in the Instructions and Regulations.
